options.label: Spell them out
options.rule: When writing centuries, spell them out. Example: le dix-neuvième siècle.

options.label: Use Arabic numerals
options.rule: When writing centuries, use Arabic numerals. Example: le 19e siècle.

options.label: Use Roman numerals
options.rule: When writing centuries, use Roman numerals. Example: le XIXe siècle.

options.label: DD.MM.YYYY
options.rule: Use the date format DD.MM.YYYY. Example: 29.02.2004.

options.label: DD/MM/YYYY
options.rule: Use the date format DD/MM/YYYY. Example: 29/02/2004.

options.label: DD month YYYY
options.rule: Use the date format DD month YYYY. Example: 29 février 2004.

options.label: YYYY.MM.DD
options.rule: Use the date format YYYY.MM.DD. Example: 2004.02.29.

options.label: YYYY/MM/DD
options.rule: Use the date format YYYY/MM/DD. Example: 2004/02/29.

options.label: Spell them out
options.rule: When writing decades, spell them out. Examples: les années soixante; les années deux mille dix.

options.label: Two digits for the 20th century, four digits otherwise
options.rule: When writing decades, abbreviate them to two digits for the 20th century but write them in four digits for other centuries. Examples: les années 60; les années 2010.

options.label: Write in four digits
options.rule: When writing decades, use four digits. Examples: les années 1960; les années 2010.

options.label: Use colons without spaces
options.rule: For hours and minutes, use numbers with colons without spaces. Example: 10:16.

options.label: Use h with regular spaces
options.rule: For hours and minutes, use numbers with the letter “h” surrounded by regular spaces. Example: 10 h 16.

options.label: Use h without spaces
options.rule: For hours and minutes, use numbers with the letter “h” without spaces. Example: 10h16.

options.label: Do not use a leading zero
options.rule: For single-digit hours, do not use a leading zero. Example: 7 h 5.

options.label: Use a leading zero
options.rule: For single-digit hours, use a leading zero. Example: 07 h 05.

options.label: Use the 12-hour clock without morning or evening markers
options.rule: Use the 12-hour clock, without specifying whether it is morning or evening. Examples: 8 h 15; 9 h 30.

options.label: Use the 12-hour clock with morning or evening markers
options.rule: Use the 12-hour clock, specifying whether it is morning or evening. Examples: 8 h 15 du matin; 9 h 30 du soir.

options.label: Use the 24-hour clock
options.rule: Use the 24-hour clock. Examples: 8 h 15; 21 h 30.

options.label: Spell out the word after the amount
options.rule: When writing currencies, spell out the word after the amount. Examples: 100 euros; 100 francs suisses.

options.label: Use the currency symbol after the amount, otherwise spell out the word
options.rule: Use the currency symbol after the amount, but spell out the word if no symbol exists. Examples: 100 €; 100 francs suisses.

options.label: Use the currency symbol after the amount, otherwise use the ISO code
options.rule: Use the currency symbol after the amount, but use the ISO 4217 code if no symbol exists. Examples: 100 €; 100 CHF.

options.label: Use the ISO 4217 code after the amount
options.rule: Use the ISO 4217 code after the amount. Examples: 100 EUR; 100 CHF.

options.label: Abbreviate with a numeral, spell out without
options.rule: For units of measure, abbreviate when used with a numeral but spell out when used without. Examples: 15 kg; quelques grammes.

options.label: Always abbreviate
options.rule: For units of measure, always abbreviate, with or without a numeral. Examples: 15 kg; quelques g.

options.label: Always spell out
options.rule: For units of measure, always spell out, with or without a numeral. Examples: 15 kilogrammes; quelques grammes.

options.label: Use curly apostrophes
options.rule: Use curly apostrophes (’). Example: J’arrive.

options.label: Use straight apostrophes
options.rule: Use straight apostrophes ('). Example: J'arrive.

options.label: Use the ellipsis character
options.rule: Use the ellipsis character (…). Example: À suivre….

options.label: Use three periods
options.rule: Use three periods (...). Example: À suivre....

options.label: Use curly quotation marks
options.rule: Use curly quotation marks (“...”). Example: “Bonjour !”.

options.label: Use straight quotation marks
options.rule: Use straight quotation marks ("..."). Example: "Bonjour !".

options.label: Use guillemets
options.rule: Use guillemets («...»). Example: « Bonjour ! ».

options.label: Do not use spaces
options.rule: On each side of the slash (/), do not use spaces. Examples: et/ou; immeuble neuf/maison ancienne.

options.label: Use spaces
options.rule: On each side of the slash (/), use spaces. Examples: et / ou; immeuble neuf / maison ancienne.

options.label: Do not use spaces unless one side has more than one word
options.rule: On each side of the slash (/), do not use spaces unless at least one of the elements it divides contains more than one word. Examples: et/ou; immeuble neuf / maison ancienne.

options.label: Do not use a space
examples: «Au choix: eau plate ou eau pétillante?»
options.rule: With specific punctuation marks (?, !, :, ;, «, and »), do not use a space. Example: «Au choix: eau plate ou eau pétillante?».

options.label: Use a non-breaking space
examples: « Au choix : eau plate ou eau pétillante ? »
options.rule: With specific punctuation marks (?, !, :, ;, «, and »), use a non-breaking space. Example: « Au choix : eau plate ou eau pétillante ? ».

options.label: Use a regular space
examples: « Au choix : eau plate ou eau pétillante ? »
options.rule: With specific punctuation marks (?, !, :, ;, «, and »), use a regular space. Example: « Au choix : eau plate ou eau pétillante ? ».

options.label: Use the degree symbol
options.rule: When abbreviating “number”, use the degree symbol (°). Example: n° 2.

options.label: Use the letter o in superscript
options.rule: When abbreviating “number”, use the letter “o” in superscript. Example: nᵒ 2.

options.label: Use no
options.rule: When abbreviating “number”, use “no”. Example: no 2.

options.label: Abbreviate personal titles
options.rule: Abbreviate personal titles. Example: M. Chirac.

options.label: Spell out personal titles
options.rule: Spell out personal titles. Example: Monsieur Chirac.

options.label: Use accents and cedillas, except on capital letters
options.rule: Use accents and cedillas, except on capital letters. Examples: Etats-Unis; Ca va ?; Façonné.

options.label: Never use accents or cedillas
options.rule: Never use accents or cedillas. Examples: Etats-Unis; Ca va ?; Faconne.

options.label: Use accents and cedillas, even on capital letters
options.rule: Use accents and cedillas, even on capital letters. Examples: États-Unis; Ça va ?; Façonné.

options.label: Use an acute accent
options.rule: For verbs that conjugate like “céder” in the future tense and conditional mood, use an acute accent (traditional spelling). Example: je considérerai.

options.label: Use a grave accent
options.rule: For verbs that conjugate like “céder” in the future tense and conditional mood, use a grave accent (reformed spelling). Example: je considèrerai.

options.label: Use an acute accent
options.rule: When the subject and the verb are inverted, use an acute accent (traditional spelling). Example: aimé-je.

options.label: Use a grave accent
options.rule: When the subject and the verb are inverted, use a grave accent (reformed spelling). Example: aimè-je.

rules.title: Complete sentences
rules.rule: Write the text in complete sentences.

options.label: Write as one word
options.rule: Write compound nouns as one word (reformed spelling). Example: un portemonnaie.

options.label: Write with a hyphen
options.rule: Write compound nouns with a hyphen (traditional spelling). Example: un porte-monnaie.

rules.title: Conjunctions
rules.rule: Never start a sentence with a coordinating conjunction.

options.label: Double the following consonant
options.rule: For verbs ending in “-eler” and “-eter”, transcribe the “è” (or [ɛ] sound) by doubling the following consonant (traditional spelling). Example: elle ruisselle.

options.label: Use a grave accent
options.rule: For verbs ending in “-eler” and “-eter”, transcribe the “è” (or [ɛ] sound) with a grave accent (reformed spelling). Example: elle ruissèle.

options.label: Do not use circumflex accents except in verbs and homophones
options.rule: For “i” and “u”, do not use circumflex accents, except in verbs and to distinguish homophones (reformed spelling). Examples: piqure; il a dû partir.

options.label: Use circumflex accents
options.rule: For “i” and “u”, use circumflex accents (traditional spelling). Examples: piqûre; il a dû partir.

rules.title: Passive voice
rules.rule: Avoid the passive voice when the agent is known.

options.label: Make “laissé” agree with the direct object
options.rule: When writing the past participle “laissé” followed by an infinitive, make “laissé” agree with the direct object complement if it appears before the verb (traditional spelling). Example: je les ai laissés partir.

options.label: Use the invariable form
options.rule: When writing the past participle “laissé” followed by an infinitive, use the invariable form “laissé” (reformed spelling). Example: je les ai laissé partir.

options.label: Use French singular and plural forms
options.rule: For foreign words, use French spelling rules for the singular and plural forms of the word (reformed spelling). Examples: un spaghetti; des spaghettis.

options.label: Use the original singular and plural forms
options.rule: For foreign words, use the singular and plural forms of the original language (traditional spelling). Examples: un spaghetto; des spaghetti.

options.label: Use hyphens
options.rule: When writing numbers in words, use hyphens (reformed spelling). Examples: deux-mille-cent-trente-et-un; quatre-vingt-deux.

options.label: Use traditional spacing and hyphenation
examples: deux mille cent trente et un
options.rule: When writing numbers in words, use hyphens between elements of a compound number that are below one hundred and not separated by “et”; otherwise, use spaces (traditional spelling). Examples: deux mille cent trente et un; quatre-vingt-deux.

options.label: Use “vous”
options.rule: When addressing the reader, use “vous”.

options.label: Use “tu”
options.rule: When addressing the reader, use “tu”.

rules.title: Anglicisms
rules.rule: Avoid using anglicisms when there is a commonly used French equivalent.

options.label: Use the long form
options.rule: When writing country names, use the long form. Example: la Confédération suisse.

options.label: Use the short form
options.rule: When writing country names, use the short form. Example: la Suisse.

options.label: Use both masculine and feminine forms
options.rule: When the gender of one or more individuals is unspecified, use both masculine and feminine forms. Example: les enseignants et les enseignantes.

options.label: Use gender-neutral terms and expressions
options.rule: When the gender of one or more individuals is unspecified, use gender-neutral terms and expressions. Example: le corps enseignant.

options.label: Use the masculine form only
options.rule: When the gender of one or more individuals is unspecified, use the masculine form only. Example: les enseignants.

options.label: Use middle dots
options.rule: When the gender of one or more individuals is unspecified, use middle dots. Example: les enseignant·e·s.

options.label: Use parentheses
options.rule: When the gender of one or more individuals is unspecified, use parentheses. Example: les enseignant(e)s.

options.label: Use periods
options.rule: When the gender of one or more individuals is unspecified, use periods. Example: les enseignant.e.s.

options.label: Place masculine nouns close to agreeing words
examples: des participantes et participants qui sont venus nombreux
options.rule: When referring to people, arrange words so that the masculine nouns are as close as possible to the words inflected to agree with them. Examples: de nombreux participants et participantes; des participantes et participants qui sont venus nombreux.

options.label: Use proximity agreement
examples: des participants et participantes qui sont venues nombreuses
options.rule: When referring to people, use the proximity agreement. Examples: de nombreux participants et participantes; des participants et participantes qui sont venues nombreuses.
